chunks: Indeed, when Jibrāʾīl descended upon the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله with the ruling of shortening, the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله said to him: “In how much is that?” He said: “In a barīd.” He said: “And how much is the barīd?” He said: “What is between the shadow of ʿAyr and the shade of Wuʿayr.” Then Banū Umayyah measured it, then divided it into twelve miles, so each mile was one thousand and five hundred cubits, and it is four farsakhs.

key_terms.بَرِيدٍ: a unit of travel distance used as the threshold here
key_terms.جَبْرَئِيلُ: the angel Jibrāʾīl who conveyed the ruling
key_terms.ذِرَاعٍ: a cubit, used to quantify the mile
key_terms.رَسُولَ اللَّهِ: the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم
key_terms.فَرَاسِخَ: parasangs; the final equivalent measure stated in the hadith
key_terms.مِيلًا: a measured mile in the described calculation

ai.seo_question: What distance requires shortening salat during travel in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith explains the basis for the ruling of shortening salat during travel by defining the travel distance in terms of a barīd. It also records a historical measurement equating that distance to four farsakhs, clarifying a practical standard used in jurisprudence.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.1302 - Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq (as) said:

"When Archangel Jibril (as) descended upon the Messenger of Allah (sw) with the ruling of shortening (the prayer), the Prophet (sw) asked him, 'For how long (a distance) is this required?'
Archangel Jibril (as) replied: 'For a barid.'
The Prophet (sw) asked: 'And what is a barid?'
Jibril said: 'The distance between the shadow of 'Ayr to the shade of Wu'ayr.'
The Banu Umayyah measured it, divided it into twelve miles, with each mile being one thousand five hundred cubits, equating to four farsakhs (parasangs).'"
